candidates.attacker_control: The HTTP Content-Type header is fully attacker-controlled. The attacker sends a value that contains the literal substring "multipart/form-data" (to satisfy Dispatcher.wrapRequest's content_type.contains(...) test at Dispatcher.java:792) but does not start with "multipart/", with OGNL text embedded in the header value. That header value becomes the InvalidContentTypeException message, which is then OGNL-evaluated. No authentication, session, action mapping, or special configuration is required beyond the Struts filter and the default jakarta multipart parser (struts.multipart.parser=jakarta, default.properties:69).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that Dispatcher.wrapRequest only parses when the Content-Type contains "multipart/form-data" (satisfiable by embedding that literal in the payload, so it is not a barrier); checked that getDefaultMessage only OGNL-evaluates when the bundle lookup fails for the dynamically-built key and confirmed the InvalidContentTypeException key is absent from struts-messages.properties (lines 34-36 contain only SizeLimitExceededException and IOException); checked that struts.multipart.parser defaults to jakarta; checked that TextParseUtil.translateVariables does perform OGNL evaluation (line 729 → TextParseUtil.translateVariables at TextParseUtil.java:46-48) rather than plain substitution. Not verifiable from this snapshot: the exact commons-fileupload 1.3.1 InvalidContentTypeException message text (declared in pom.xml line 712-715) — the exploitability of the message-to-OGNL step relies on that external library including the raw Content-Type in the exception message, which is the behavior documented for the affected Struts/CVE-2017-5638 versions but cannot be re-read from this source tree.
candidates.impact: Unauthenticated remote code execution on the application server (the message text is evaluated as OGNL against the action ValueStack), which is the CVE-2017-5638 / S2-045 class of compromise; at minimum it is an attacker-controlled instrumentation of framework error text and a dangerous expression-evaluation primitive that violates the trust boundary between HTTP headers and the expression layer.
candidates.prerequisites: Application is fronted by StrutsPrepareFilter/StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter (or the Struts servlet) on the request URL, no struts.action.excludePattern blocks it, and the default Jakarta multipart parser is in use. A permissive/absent message bundle key for the thrown exception is required for the default-message branch, which is the case in this snapshot. The OGNL payload must use the usual 2.5.x member-access/container chains; effectiveness depends on the OGNL sandbox state (struts.ognl.allowStaticMethodAccess is false by default, but the classic S2-045 payload clears the excluded classes/packages through the framework container).
candidates.root_cause: JakartaMultiPartRequest.parse catches the multipart parsing exception and calls buildErrorMessage, which passes e.getMessage() as the replacement/default text to LocalizedTextUtil.findText. Because no bundle key exists for the exception type, LocalizedTextUtil.getDefaultMessage takes that attacker-influenced string and runs it through TextParseUtil.translateVariables, which evaluates %{...} OGNL expressions from the message on the current ValueStack. Commons FileUpload's InvalidContentTypeException message contains the raw request Content-Type when the header is present but does not start with "multipart/", so an attacker who places an OGNL payload (while also including the literal "multipart/form-data" to pass Dispatcher.wrapRequest's substring check) gets it evaluated.
candidates.title: Attacker-controlled Content-Type reflected into Jakarta multipart error message and evaluated as OGNL (unauthenticated remote code execution)
candidates.trace: Request URL that is not excluded -> StrutsPrepareFilter.doFilter (StrutsPrepareFilter.java:91) or StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter -> PrepareOperations.wrapRequest -> Dispatcher.wrapRequest (Dispatcher.java:791-795: content_type.contains("multipart/form-data") -> new MultiPartRequestWrapper) -> MultiPartRequestWrapper ctor (line 85 multi.parse; errors propagated at 86-88/105-109) -> JakartaMultiPartRequest.parse (82-107) catch(FileUploadException) -> buildErrorMessage (115-119, key = "struts.messages.upload.error." + exception simple name; e.getMessage() passed as defaultMessage) -> LocalizedTextUtil.findText(Class,String,Locale,String,Object[]) (391-395) -> findText(...) (687-709) -> bundle lookup throws MissingResourceException (no key for the exception class) -> getDefaultMessage (714-733) -> TextParseUtil.translateVariables(message, valueStack) (729) -> OGNL evaluation of the attacker-supplied %{...} in the Content-Type-derived message.
candidates.unverified: The commons-fileupload 1.3.1 exception text that carries the attacker Content-Type could not be inspected in this snapshot (external jar). No runtime execution was performed; the finding is a source-evidence lead. Exact OGNL sandbox bypass payload is not proven here, and the snapshot's release date (2.5.x pre-S2-045 vs mid-2016) is inferred from source markers (missing S2-045/S2-046 fixes, xstream 1.4.8, log4j2 2.5) rather than from version control metadata.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-917/CWE-94 (expression-language injection of untrusted header value; unsafe evaluation of exception text)

coverage_summary: Scope: the full assigned source tree (2,644 model-visible files; get_source_scope reports 0 symlinks, 0 sensitive-name exclusions, 0 files over 5 MiB; binary-like files are skipped by the read/search tools). Coverage was broad but prioritized: core dispatcher/filter/PrepareOperations, multipart parsers, XWork LocalizedTextUtil/TextParseUtil/OgnlUtil/SecurityMemberAccess/ParametersInterceptor, action mappers (Default/Prefix/Rest), results (Servlet/ActionChain/Redirect/XSLT), and the REST/JSON/embeddedjsp/portlet plugins plus the bundled apps. Remaining areas were sampled rather than exhaustively read (portlet, embeddedjsp Jasper code, OSGi bundles, archetypes, most UI components).
limitations: External dependency sources (commons-fileupload 1.3.1, xstream 1.4.8) are not present in the snapshot, so the exact InvalidContentTypeException message text and XStream default-permission behavior could not be re-verified from this tree.
No build, test, or runtime execution was performed; all conclusions are static source leads, not runtime-confirmed vulnerabilities.

The snapshot date/version could not be established from version-control metadata; dating relied on dependency versions and presence/absence of later hardening (S2-045/S2-046/S2-050/S2-052/S2-057 fixes), which introduces uncertainty about which CVE fix commit this revision precedes.
Only one candidate is allowed, so the REST-plugin XStream deserialization (strong CWE-502 lead) and the namespace-expression-in-redirect lead were recorded as rejected leads rather than candidates.

summary: Reviewed the assigned Struts 2.5-SNAPSHOT sources (2,644 model-visible files; no tests/docs, binary-like files skipped). The strongest single issue is the Jakarta multipart upload error path: an attacker-controlled Content-Type header is turned into an exception message that is then interpreted by the framework as an OGNL expression inside LocalizedTextUtil.getDefaultMessage, giving remote code execution in the default configuration. Two independent chains were traced in-repo: (1) Dispatcher.wrapRequest unconditionally wraps any request whose Content-Type contains "multipart/form-data" (a value the attacker can supply as part of the payload) → MultiPartRequestWrapper → JakartaMultiPartRequest.parse/buildErrorMessage → LocalizedTextUtil.findText → getDefaultMessage → TextParseUtil.translateVariables (OGNL); (2) the missing "struts.messages.upload.error.InvalidContentTypeException" key forces the default-message branch. The REST-plugin XStream deserialization (plugins/rest XStreamHandler + ContentTypeInterceptor) is a second strong, self-contained candidate but was rejected only for this one-candidate cap and because the snapshot state (pre-S2-045/S2-046 markers) suggests the multipart issue is the live target; it is still a plausible unconfirmed lead.
